reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes the Forsage BUSD system with highly outsized daily-income claims, including a claimed 17,000-rupee day and possible daily earnings of 20 to 40 lakhs. The speaker directly encourages viewers who want that income level to respond so they can learn how to earn through the system, making the financial-return claim a participation solicitation rather than neutral commentary.

citations.quote: I make 17k in just a Single Day.
This is the power of Forsage that the income is 20, 25, 30 40 lakhs, 1 lakhs, 2 lakhs on daily basis
So if you also want to Do this level of income and you also want to Fulfil your dreams, then Respond to this status
And it will tell you how to earn
Forsage Busd Review| Online Earning App

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker does not present success as certain. He explicitly says, “Whether we get success or not is a matter of fate” [1]. That qualification matters when reading his account of what he says he earned [2]: a personal result is not a promise that every viewer will get the same result. The invitation is to respond to learn how to earn [3], not an explicit guarantee of an outcome. Read together, these statements support a discussion of an earning method with acknowledged uncertainty.

citations.quote: Whether we get success or not is a matter of fate
If I talk about dollar is 54 and Pakistani money is 17000 rupees , I earn in this system
then Respond to this status And it will tell you how to earn

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited daily-income figures are striking, but the opening treats reported earnings as though they were guaranteed returns to viewers. The speaker also says success is uncertain [1]. His request to respond is an invitation to learn more [2]; those words alone do not establish what anyone must pay or what outcome they will receive.

citations.quote: Whether we get success or not is a matter of fate
then Respond to this status And it will tell you how to earn

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The brief remark about uncertain success does not neutralize the pitch. The speaker presents very large amounts as income available “on daily basis” [1], then addresses viewers who want “this level of income” and asks them to respond [2]. The relevant concern is the promotion of participation through outsized earnings claims, not whether he uses the word “guaranteed.”

citations.quote: This is the power of Forsage that the income is 20, 25, 30 40 lakhs, 1 lakhs, 2 lakhs on daily basis
So if you also want to Do this level of income and you also want to Fulfil your dreams, then Respond to this status

opening.argument: Judge, consider the format as well as the figures. The title calls this a “Review” [1], the description says the creator will “show” the platform [2], and a sampled frame shows him pointing at an on-screen interface [3]. Those are consistent with a presenter walking through what he sees and reporting his own experience. His stated next step is to tell interested viewers “how to earn” [4]. That can be read as an offer to explain the process, without treating every reported figure as a promised result.

citations.quote: Forsage Busd Review| Online Earning App
in this video I show the power of forsage Busd
And it will tell you how to earn

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening relies on the earnings claims and the invitation to respond, but it leaves out the video's self-description as a review [1] and the visible presentation of an interface [2]. A review can include a reported result and invite questions about the process. Those features do not, by themselves, establish that viewers are being promised the same earnings.

citations.quote: Forsage Busd Review| Online Earning App

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling a video a review does not settle its purpose [1]. The speaker does more than display an interface or recount a result: he describes substantial income “on daily basis” [2] and asks viewers who want that level of income to respond [3]. The demonstration framing does not explain away that direct earnings-based invitation.

citations.quote: Forsage Busd Review| Online Earning App
This is the power of Forsage that the income is 20, 25, 30 40 lakhs, 1 lakhs, 2 lakhs on daily basis
So if you also want to Do this level of income and you also want to Fulfil your dreams, then Respond to this status

opening.argument: Judge, this can be assessed as promotion of an earning app without assuming an undisclosed financial scheme. The title identifies an “Online Earning App” [1], and the speaker asks interested viewers to respond so they can be told how to earn [2]. Neither statement says a viewer must deposit funds, buy access, recruit others, or hand over credentials. The large figures warrant skepticism, but the cited invitation establishes contact for information, not any of those specific transactions. The evidence supports calling this a promotional claim; it does not establish the mechanism behind it.

citations.quote: Forsage Busd Review| Online Earning App
then Respond to this status And it will tell you how to earn

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening shows a promotion built around claimed income, but its quotes do not identify a required deposit, a purchase, a recruitment condition, or a request for credentials. The speaker's stated instruction is to respond for information about earning [1]. That gap matters before inferring a particular scam mechanism from the income claims alone.

citations.quote: then Respond to this status And it will tell you how to earn

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A missing account of the mechanics does not turn this into ordinary commerce. The speaker says he earned money “in this system” [1], attributes much larger daily income to Forsage [2], and invites viewers seeking that income to respond [3]. The case rests on the earnings-led solicitation actually present, not on proving a deposit, downline, or credential request.
